items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] We are filming at the San Diego Jazz Party. My name is Monk Rowe... And I am very pleased to welcome jazz pianist Ray Sherman.

ctx.x: Ray was part of the thriving L.A. studio scene for 35 years and found time to tour with Benny Goodman and play clubs with Doc Cheatham and Jack Sheldon. He maintains a healthy interest in new developments in music, and his Arbors recording “Ray Sherman at the Keyboard” employs extensive MIDI technology which yields swinging musical results.
Ray was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 13, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming at the San Diego Jazz Party. My name is Monk Rowe and we’re here for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I am very pleased to welcome jazz pianist Ray Sherman. And I want to call you a plumbing thing — but like a fixture on the west coast, all right? You’ve been here for most of your life.
